newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end higher, crown flat.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end higher, crown flat.

text.p: Swedish bond yields closed higher on Tuesday on continued worries that a French snap election might disrupt the timetable for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU), while the crown ended largely unchanged.
Domestic worries concerned the minority Social Democratic government's view on a Swedish link to EMU. Finance Minister Erik Asbrink is supposed to disclose the government's opinion in May.
* Six-month T-bill rate rises three basis points to 4.19 pct.
* Ten-year bond yield jumps eight basis points to 7.33 pct.
* Crown flat at 4.4840 to mark vs 4.4875 late on Monday.

STOCKHOLM, April 22 (Reuter) - Swedish bond yields closed higher on Tuesday on continued worries that a French election might disrupt the timetable for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU). The crown ended largely unchanged.
Domestic worries concerned the minority Social Democratic government's view on a Swedish link to EMU. Finance Minister Erik Asbrink is supposed to disclose the government's opinion in May.
"The Social Democrats' view on EMU is crucial for whether we will see a rally in the crown or not," a dealer said, adding that the crown was also depressed by higher bond yields.

Swedes, in general, are fairly negative to both the European Union (EU) and EMU and the government needs to regain voter support ahead of general elections in September 1998. Market players are nervous about what the government will say.
The crown ended largely unchanged at 4.4840 to the mark compared to 4.4875 late on Monday.
Six month T-bill rate rose three basis points to 4.19 percent and the ten-year bond yield jumped eight basis points to 7.33 percent.
